name: NY-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Malliotakis holds roughly a 40-to-1 fundraising advantage with $2.8 million on hand
The district leans about ten points Republican, favoring the incumbent party
Prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 4 percent chance
No public polls and no meaningful outside spending on either side
model.rationale: An incumbent in a district that leans ten points Republican, armed with a massive cash advantage over a minimally funded challenger and priced near 95 percent by markets, is a very strong favorite. No polling or headline evidence suggests Democratic traction, so the forecast sits at the safe end of the Republican column.
model.watch: Any late public polling or outside spending entering the district could test whether the margin truly extends beyond fifteen points.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Rep. Nicole Malliotakis seeks re-election in a Staten Island-based district that leans about ten points Republican. She enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised $2.75 million and holding $2.8 million on hand, against roughly $68,000 raised by Democratic challenger Michael DeCillis. Neither side shows meaningful outside spending.

No public polling is available in this race, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a four percent chance of winning. The district's partisan lean, the incumbent's overwhelming money edge, and the absence of any visible Democratic traction point to a comfortable Malliotakis victory with an expected margin in the mid-teens. The race sits at the safer end of the Republican column, though without surveys the estimate rests on fundamentals, fundraising, and market pricing.
